{{Short description|Incentivized statistical survey}}
{{Refimprove|date=March 2008}}

A '''paid''' or '''incentivized survey''' is a type of [[statistical survey]] where the participants/members are rewarded through an incentive program, generally entry into a [[sweepstakes]] program or a small cash reward, for completing one or more surveys.

== Details ==

A paid survey is used to collect quantitative information about the participants' personal and economic habits set against their particular [[demographic]].

Legitimate surveys are usually unpaid (as with a [[Gallup poll]]) or incentivized. Surveys where the respondent must pay or purchase products to join a panel are generally scams, as are sites that disappear before paying the participants.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scambusters.org/onlinesurveys2.html |title=The Real Deal About Online Survey Scams |publisher=Scambusters |access-date=2012-02-05}}</ref> Legitimate surveys do not need [[credit card]] information from respondents.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.surveycompare.net/paid-surveys/learn-avoid-scam-survey-sites/ |title=How to Avoid Scam Survey Sites |publisher=SurveyCompare |access-date=2012-10-16}}</ref>
